html:
The Serrano are a Native American people of southern California, from the San Bernardino Mountains and the nearby Mojave Desert. Their Spanish name means "mountaineers".

They speak a Takic language of the Uto-Aztecan family, related to those of the Cahuilla and the Tongva. They lived in small clan villages, gathering acorns, pinyon nuts and mesquite and hunting deer and small game.

From the late 1700s Spanish missions drew many Serrano from the valleys to Mission San Gabriel. Mexican ranchers and then American settlers took the rest of the lowlands. Today their descendants belong to the San Manuel Band and to the Morongo and other reservations.
